question: Compare the cloud computing approaches of AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure in terms of service model, infrastructure management, scalability, and application deployment.
Compare the compute capabilities provided by AWS EC2 and Lambda, Google App Engine, and Azure Virtual Machines and Functions, and explain how they support different application workloads.
Compare the storage and data management capabilities of AWS, Google App Engine integrated Google Cloud services, and Microsoft Azure.
Explain how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure provide scalability and handle changing application traffic.
Compare how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure reduce infrastructure management while supporting application development and deployment.
Compare the database services available through AWS, Google App Engine integrated services, and Microsoft Azure, including relational, NoSQL, and caching options.
Explain how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure support secure cloud applications through identity, access control, encryption, network protection, and platform security capabilities.
Compare the networking, load balancing, and content delivery capabilities described for AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure.
Explain how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure support application monitoring, logging, deployment management, and operational reliability.
Compare the developer and DevOps capabilities of AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure for building, deploying, automating, and maintaining cloud applications.
Explain how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure can support scalable web applications, APIs, backend services, and microservice-based applications.
Compare how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure support data-intensive applications using storage, databases, analytics, and data processing services.

Explain how AWS and Microsoft Azure support artificial intelligence and machine learning workloads, and describe how applications hosted using Google App Engine can use integrated Google Cloud services.
Compare the IoT and edge computing capabilities described for AWS and Microsoft Azure, and explain how Google App Engine can participate as an application backend for connected applications.
Compare AWS and Microsoft Azure approaches to hybrid and edge computing, including AWS Outposts, Snowball, and Wavelength and Azure Arc, Azure Stack, and Azure VMware Solution.
Explain the differences between infrastructure-oriented cloud services such as AWS EC2 and Azure Virtual Machines and a managed Platform-as-a-Service such as Google App Engine.
Compare server-based, serverless, and managed application hosting approaches using examples from AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure.
Explain how automatic scaling works across AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure and how scalability benefits applications experiencing variable workloads.
Compare the advantages of AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure for organizations requiring scalable infrastructure, managed services, application hosting, data management, and security.

Discuss the limitations and management trade-offs of using highly managed cloud platforms such as Google App Engine compared with the broader infrastructure and platform services available in AWS and Microsoft Azure.
Explain how compute, storage, databases, networking, and security services work together to support a complete cloud application, using examples from AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure.
Compare how AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure can support enterprise applications, e-commerce systems, APIs, data processing applications, and other scalable cloud workloads.

Explain how cloud platforms combine managed infrastructure, automatic scaling, load balancing, monitoring, security, and data services to improve application availability and reduce operational effort.
Compare AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure in terms of compute or application hosting, storage, databases, networking, security, analytics, scalability, and developer support.

Using AWS, Google App Engine, and Microsoft Azure as examples, explain how modern cloud platforms provide end-to-end support for application development, deployment, scalability, data management, security, monitoring, analytics, and different application workloads.
